text: How should the music be delivered?
context: One 16 MB file is downloaded whole within seconds by Firefox and Safari on a fast connection, even if the player leaves after a minute. Chrome takes about 6 MB.

options.label: Four files, one per track, with the fades built in
options.rationale: A first listen costs 1.4 to 3.4 MB, a session can start on a different track, and no fading script is needed on iPhone. Needs a small change to the mix script.

options.label: One file, the mix as it is
options.rationale: Simplest and exactly your mix, but 6 to 16 MB on a first listen and it always opens the same way.

options.label: Music only as a download the player asks for
options.rationale: Cheapest, but most players would never hear it.

text: Which quality should the music ship at?
context: Sizes for all four tracks, measured: Opus 64 is 10.8 MB, Opus 96 is 16.3 MB. iPhones use a separate AAC copy (96 kbps, 16.2 MB).

options.label: Opus 64 and AAC 96, after you listen
options.rationale: A third smaller. Best if you cannot tell the difference in headphones; please compare on Unraveling.

options.label: Opus 96 and AAC 96
options.rationale: Closer to the usual guideline, 5.5 MB more in total.

options.label: Opus 96 and AAC 128
options.rationale: Nearest to your current files, 16 to 21 MB.

text: What should happen with sound on a first visit?
context: Browsers do not allow sound before a click.

options.label: Music starts with the first campaign, at a modest level, with a notice and a mute button
options.rationale: Players hear it, and one press stops it.

options.label: Everything starts off until the player turns it on
options.rationale: Never annoys, but most players will not find it.

options.label: Effects on, music off
options.rationale: A middle path that hides the music.

text: Which sounds should we make now?
context: Fourteen candidates are in the audition board. Every licence was checked; none has been listened to by us.

options.label: Your eight, plus a soft refused tick and one distant-guns sound when the battle report opens
options.rationale: Covers your list and gives the report some weight, about 0.1 MB in all.

options.label: Only your eight
options.rationale: Fewest sounds to tire of.

options.label: Your eight plus victory, defeat and weather
options.rationale: More atmosphere, and more to license and tune.

text: How strict should the limits on repeated sounds be?
context: Ten rail orders at once would be ten whistles and about 5 dB over the maximum, which crackles. Try both in the mix lab.

options.label: Strict: one sound per action, a special sound at most every four seconds, then a quiet tick
options.rationale: Special sounds stay special. Four seconds is a starting value to tune by ear.

options.label: Looser: special sounds every second or so
options.rationale: Livelier, and tires faster.

options.label: Special sounds only for the first order of each kind each turn
options.rationale: Calmest, and the player may wonder why a later train is silent.

text: In games where two people share one device, should order sounds reveal what was ordered?
context: A train whistle tells the other player that a rail move was made.

options.label: Use the same plain tick for every order when people share a device
options.rationale: Keeps plans secret, with no cost in single-player.

options.label: Always play the special sounds
options.rationale: Simplest, but leaks plans.

options.label: Let the players choose in Settings
options.rationale: Fair, but one more option most will not see.

text: When should the detailed map picture load?
context: It is 1.8 MB of the 3.1 MB a new player downloads, and it loads before anyone zooms in.

options.label: Only when the player zooms in, or when idle on a fast connection
options.rationale: Cuts up to 59% for players who do not zoom. A zoom may be soft for a moment.

options.label: As now, at the start of the campaign
options.rationale: Sharp at once, and the largest cost in the game.

options.label: On zoom, and re-encode it smaller
options.rationale: A further 0.8 MB or so in all, but the map must be looked at and the visual tests refreshed.

text: Should a download size limit stop a build?
context: A limit exists and is already missed (159.4 kB against 155 kB for the first script), but nothing runs the check.

options.label: Yes, after moving the rules and computer player out of the first script, and cover audio and images too
options.rationale: Keeps growth visible, and the limit stays where you set it.

options.label: Yes, from today, blocking
options.rationale: Nothing else can merge until the miss is fixed.

options.label: Report only
options.rationale: Easy, and easily ignored, as now.
